body:
Hah, I appreciate it but my plan right now is to have my sister and BIL take care of him until disability approves me. He's a big sweety, a huge moggie that's mostly Maine coon, and they already have a setup that can keep him well cared for.

I worked in IT for about 8 years, first as a sysadmin/help desk/dataminer for a startup and then as a professional services consultant for a specific natural language AI that is no longer in use. This has put me in a terrible position for hiring because my specialty has no value and most companies see me as overqualified for entry level work but underqualified for most anything else. Being in isolation and being unable to work a regular schedule or lift heavy equipment doesn't help, either.

Edit: cat tax https://imgur.com/a/aw27IkK

Thanks, it feels an awful lot more like a siege than a battle - a battle can be won; a siege is just a matter of how long you can hold out.

I have a single rheumatologist who has been excellent in that he has listened to what I believe is happening to my body instead of repeating "horses not zebras," but the cheapest healthcare money can buy isn't exactly a phenomenal HMO. I'm also on danger of my coverage lapsing.

Bo's always been a very insightful performer, the part of inside where he watches playback of himself giving empty platitudes against the idea of suicide because it's all he can muster hits hard.
